intro: No INS 204 past papers were found in the course folder. These exam-style questions were written for practice from the lecture notes and slides; they are not from a past paper.

papers.paper: Exam-style questions, not from a past paper: written for this app from the INS 204 lecture notes and slides
papers.source: Written for this app from the INS 204 lecture notes and slides, because no past papers were found for the course

questions.text: a) Distinguish between systems analysis and systems design. (4 marks) b) Define a system and explain six elements of a system. (8 marks) c) State the four attributes of a systems analyst. (3 marks)
Explain, with examples, the following types of systems: (i) open and closed (ii) deterministic, probabilistic and random (iii) adaptive and non-adaptive. (15 marks)
a) List and explain the seven phases of the SDLC. (10 marks) b) Describe three methods of changing over from an old system to a new one, stating one advantage of each. (5 marks)
a) Compare the waterfall, incremental and spiral models. (9 marks) b) What are CASE tools? State three of their uses. (6 marks)
a) Distinguish functional from non-functional requirements, with two examples of each. (6 marks) b) Describe four fact-finding techniques, stating when each is most suitable. (9 marks)
a) Explain the five types of feasibility. (10 marks) b) Distinguish tangible from intangible costs and benefits, and name three methods of cost-benefit analysis. (5 marks)
a) Name and describe the four symbols used in data flow diagrams. (8 marks) b) State four rules for constructing DFDs, and explain 'black hole' and 'miracle'. (7 marks)

For a university course registration system in which students submit registration forms, the system checks them against the course catalogue and sends confirmation slips, draw a context diagram and a first-level DFD. Explain how the two diagrams are balanced. (15 marks)
a) Distinguish candidate, primary, alternate, foreign and surrogate keys. (8 marks) b) Explain entity and referential integrity. (4 marks) c) State the rules of 1NF, 2NF and 3NF. (3 marks)

a) Compare two-tier and three-tier architectures, and give four benefits of three-tier architecture. (9 marks) b) Explain encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction with examples. (6 marks)

a) State five objectives of input design. (5 marks) b) Distinguish validation from verification, and client-side from server-side validation. (6 marks) c) Distinguish operational, management and analytical reports. (4 marks)
